thiazole leitropsin (1), which has a thiazole ring in place of the pyridine of leitropsin, binds to a DNA decamer d-[CGCAATTCGC]2 in a 1:1 stoichiometry, with its thiazole ring intercalating between two adjacent adenine bases in the decamer and the rest of its structure occupying the minor groove of this DNA decamer.
the thiazolyl moiety of the lexitropic ligand intercalates between the dA4.A6 base pairs of the decamer and the rest of ligand resides in minor groove of the DNA.

the thiazolylexitropsin (TLX) intercalates into the AATT sequence of a decadeoxyribonuleotide, and that the N-formy (amino) and amidinium termini of the TLX lie in the major and minor grooves, respectively, of the decamer.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a novel class of DNA binding ligands, which have been shown to have a high affinity for AT rich DNA sequences and to be selective for the 5'-ATTA sequence.

the structural and dynamic aspects and the mechanism of binding of the GC site-avoider, thiazole leitropsin, to a decanucleotide containing the 5'-ATT sequence, a preferred binding sequence in leitropsin-DNA complexes.
